instructions: Assess only the listed primary candidates in a fresh invocation. Read their dialogue first, then the exact card; use the alternate only to judge meaningful differentiation. Supply six criterion ratings with specific turn evidence and full coach-2.0 findings. Do not invent missing backstory or assume earlier approval. No writer scores or rationales are supplied. Report real reservations and failures. Totals are calculated in code.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

card.title: Apologize to Reality
card.instruction: Get someone to apologize to an object, rule, place, or idea for violating its impossible expectations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before your caretaker interview, apologise to that chair. You sat without its consent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It can't say yes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell it you're sorry for taking silence as permission.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sorry, chair. I'll stand for the interview.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then apologise for making it redundant. You're applying to care for furniture, and your first solution is to leave it without a job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Welcome to our inn. Please apologise to the doorway for knocking after you arrived.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I had to get here to knock.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It expected advance notice from your knuckles. Explain that you're sorry.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sorry, doorway. I did phone ahead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then apologise for telling the telephone first. It had to hear about its own visitor secondhand.

card.title: Approve the Impossible Plan
card.instruction: Get someone to formally approve a plan whose logic becomes stranger each time it is explained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As venue manager, will you approve storing Tuesday's rain in this cup? The wedding needs a dry lawn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tuesday hasn't happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. We'll catch the rain before it learns how to fall.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have another wedding Wednesday. What if it leaks overnight?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll seal it with Thursday's drought. Sign for two dry weddings; I'll invoice the drought after it happens.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Inspector, please approve our invisible landing. The museum opens Monday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's nothing supporting it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've budgeted enough confidence to hold twenty visitors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How am I supposed to certify confidence?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sign under 'load-bearing.' Your professional certainty will support the inspectors too, so we won't need scaffolding for the next inspection.

card.title: You Handle the Impossible Part
card.instruction: Make someone accept responsibility for the one part of the plan that cannot reasonably be done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For tonight's courtyard film, you fold the moon; I'll switch off the lamps.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How do I fold the moon?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with the crescent. It already has a crease.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the lamps. You handle the sky.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll do lamps, chairs and projector if you'll own the moon. Can I tell the audience we're waiting for your blackout?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put yesterday's missing hour in this jar before lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Time doesn't fit in jars.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then loosen the lid. Don't make the opening smaller than necessary.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You do it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm labelling. We mustn't confuse it with tomorrow.

card.title: What Rule Did I Miss?
card.instruction: Find the hidden rule that makes the strange situation consistent, practical, or at least survivable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What keeps the soup inside that upside-down bowl?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've never seen it either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then turn the spoon over. Let's test which thing owns down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The soup followed the spoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the spoon sets the direction. Point it into the sink before we try putting it down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your shadow moved before you. What changed?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was thinking of leaving, but I can't find the exit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Think about that bench without moving. Does it turn?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's gone to the bench. I'm still here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It seems to follow your intentions. Think about the exit again; let's follow slowly and see whether it knows the way.
